description: First contact with programming: thinking in algorithms, writing them as pseudocode and flowcharts, then as real code with variables, control flow, functions and a first look at objects. Taught to the depth of a leading first programming course, with a working program every week.
modelledOn: Zelle, Python Programming: An Introduction to Computer Science
Guttag, Introduction to Computation and Programming
Roberts, The Art and Science of Java
outcomes: Explain how source code becomes a running program and the roles of compilers, interpreters and linkers.
Design an algorithm for a stated problem and express it as pseudocode and a flowchart before coding.
Write programs that use variables, expressions, selection and loops correctly, and trace them by hand.
Decompose a program into functions with clear parameters and return values.
Explain objects, classes, attributes and methods and use simple objects in a program.
Find and fix syntax, runtime and logic errors with a systematic debugging method and tests.

units.title: Programs, languages and translators
topics: What a program is; machine code, low-level and high-level languages; why there are many languages
Compilers, interpreters, assemblers and linkers; the edit-run-debug loop
Setting up an editor and running a first program; printing and reading input
Programming vocabulary: source, syntax, semantics, statement, expression, bug

units.title: Algorithms, pseudocode and flowcharts
topics: Properties of an algorithm: finite, definite, effective; inputs and outputs
Pseudocode conventions; flowchart symbols for process, decision, loop, input/output
Tracing an algorithm with a trace table
Everyday algorithms: making change in cedis, computing a GPA, finding the largest of three numbers
From flowchart to code and back

units.title: Data: character set, constants, types, variables
topics: Character set, identifiers, keywords and naming rules
Literals and constants; integer, floating-point, character, string and boolean types
Variables, declaration, assignment and memory as named boxes
Type conversion and casting; integer division and rounding surprises
Input, output and formatting numbers and strings

units.title: Operators and expressions
topics: Arithmetic, relational, logical, assignment and increment operators
Precedence and associativity; evaluating expressions by hand
Boolean expressions and short-circuit evaluation
Common expression errors: off-by-one, mixing types, confusing = and ==

units.title: Selection
topics: if, if-else, else-if ladders and nested ifs
switch statements and when to prefer them
Designing conditions: grade bands, tax brackets, leap years
Testing every branch; boundary values

units.title: Iteration
topics: while, do-while and for loops; loop variable, condition, update
Counting, summing, averaging and finding maxima in a loop
Sentinel-controlled and flag-controlled loops; break and continue
Nested loops: multiplication tables, patterns, simple matrices
Infinite loops and termination; choosing the right loop

units.title: Functions and program structure
topics: Defining and calling functions; parameters, arguments, return values
Scope and lifetime of variables; local and global
Decomposition and stepwise refinement; top-down design
Library functions: maths, strings, random numbers
Introduction to recursion: factorial and Fibonacci

units.title: Collections and strings
topics: Arrays and lists: indexing, traversal, searching, finding min and max
Strings as sequences of characters; common string operations
Reading and writing a simple text file
Simple sorting by hand: bubble sort and selection sort

units.title: Basic object-oriented concepts
topics: Objects as data plus behaviour; classes as blueprints
Attributes and methods; creating and using objects
Encapsulation and why it matters; a Student or BankAccount class
Objects already met: strings, lists, files

units.title: Identifying and fixing errors
topics: Syntax, runtime and logic errors and how each shows itself
Reading error messages and stack traces
Debugging strategy: reproduce, isolate, hypothesise, test; print statements and a debugger
Writing test cases before and after fixing; defensive input checking
Code style, comments and documentation

schedule.title: First programs and vocabulary
schedule.exercise: Write a short glossary of ten programming terms with a one-line example of each from your first program.

tasks.title: Run a first program that prints a greeting, then change it to read your name and print it back, checking the output
Find and label the syntax error, runtime error and logic error in three given short programs and fix each
Compile or interpret a program in stages, introduce a deliberate mistake at each stage, and record what the tool reports

schedule.title: Algorithms and flowcharts
schedule.exercise: Write pseudocode and a flowchart for finding the average of five exam marks and trace it with a sample input.

tasks.title: Trace a given algorithm for the sum of the digits of a number with a trace table for the inputs 523 and 9040
Convert pseudocode for finding the larger of two numbers into code and test it with four inputs, including equal values
Write an algorithm that decides whether a number is prime, then test its finiteness and correctness on 10 inputs including 0 and 1

schedule.title: Everyday algorithms
schedule.exercise: Describe, in pseudocode and a flowchart, how to give change in cedis for a purchase, including the smallest notes and coins.

tasks.title: Write a program that finds the largest of three numbers and test it with six inputs, including ties
Compute a student's GPA from five course grades and credit hours, and verify the result with two worked examples
Turn a flowchart for giving change in cedis into code, then redraw the flowchart from your finished code and compare

schedule.title: Types, variables and input
schedule.exercise: Explain with five examples how integer division and floating-point rounding can surprise a beginner.

tasks.title: Declare variables of five types, assign values, print each with its type and swap two variables using a third
Convert user input from text to numbers, compute an average of three marks and show the effect of integer division and rounding
Read a name, price and quantity from the user and print a formatted receipt with two decimal places and aligned columns

schedule.title: Operators and expressions
schedule.exercise: Evaluate ten expressions by hand using precedence rules, then check each with the computer and explain any mismatch.

tasks.title: Evaluate five arithmetic expressions by hand, run them in code, and explain every step where precedence changed the result
Test a boolean expression with short-circuit evaluation where the second part would divide by zero, and show it is skipped
Find and fix five seeded expression bugs: off-by-one, mixed types, = versus == and wrong operator precedence, with a test for each

schedule.title: Decisions
schedule.exercise: Write the decision table and code for a tax bracket calculator and list the boundary values you would test.

tasks.title: Write an if-else ladder that gives a letter grade for a mark from 0 to 100, and test it at every band boundary
Decide whether a year is a leap year using nested conditions, and test with 1900, 2000, 2024 and 2023
Write a tax bracket calculator with four bands and design a test table that exercises every branch and each boundary value

schedule.title: Loops
schedule.exercise: Use a trace table to show how a while loop sums the numbers from 1 to 5, then say what changes if the condition uses less than instead of less than or equal.

tasks.title: Write for and while loops that print the numbers 1 to 10 and the even numbers up to 20, and compare their output
Read a list of marks and compute their sum, average, maximum and minimum in one pass through a loop
Write a sentinel-controlled loop that reads marks until -1 is typed, ignoring invalid values with continue and stopping early with break

schedule.title: Nested loops and termination
schedule.exercise: Predict the output of three nested loop programs by hand, then run them and explain any difference.

tasks.title: Print a multiplication table for 1 to 9 and a right-angled triangle of stars using nested loops
Find three infinite loops in given programs, explain why they never end and fix each so it terminates
Print a diamond pattern of height 7 and the transpose of a 3x4 matrix using nested loops, with a test for another size

schedule.title: Functions
schedule.exercise: Break a program that reports class statistics into five functions, drawing a top-down decomposition chart before coding.

tasks.title: Write a function that returns the area of a rectangle and call it three times with different arguments, printing each result
Run a program with a local and a global variable of the same name and predict, then check, the value printed in each place
Decompose a student report program into input, calculate and display functions, and test each function on its own before combining them

schedule.title: Libraries and recursion
schedule.exercise: Trace the calls of a recursive factorial of 4 on paper, showing the stack of waiting calls and the return values.

tasks.title: Use maths, string and random library functions to roll a die 20 times, round a value and change a string to upper case
Step through recursive factorial and Fibonacci in the visualiser, record the call stack at its deepest point and count the calls for Fibonacci of 6
Write recursive and loop versions of Fibonacci and compare their results and run time for n up to 30, explaining the difference

schedule.title: Lists, strings, files and sorting
schedule.exercise: Describe how bubble sort and selection sort differ, using the same five numbers and showing every pass.

tasks.title: Store ten marks in a list, then find the position and value of the minimum and maximum and search for a given mark
Read a text file of student names and marks, compute the average, and write those above average to a new file
Step bubble sort and selection sort through the same 8 numbers, count the comparisons and swaps of each, and explain which does less work

schedule.title: Objects and classes
schedule.exercise: Design a BankAccount class on paper with its attributes and methods, and explain what it hides from the user.

tasks.title: Define a Student class with name and mark attributes, create three objects and print each one's details
Write a BankAccount class with deposit and withdraw methods that refuses overdrafts, and test it with five transactions
Find five objects already used in earlier programs, such as strings, lists and files, call two methods on each, and explain what each one bundles

schedule.title: Debugging and good practice
schedule.exercise: Write a debugging log for one bug: how you reproduced it, what you suspected, the fix and the test you added.

tasks.title: Read three error messages and stack traces, state the file, line and cause of each, and fix the programs
Find and fix four seeded bugs in a grade calculator using reproduction, print statements and a debugger, and record the cause of each
Write test cases for a function before fixing a bug, add input checking for bad values, and show the tests pass after the fix
